item.title: copilot-cli: 1.0.101
item.description:
Release v1.0.101 adds several CLI and MCP workflow fixes, including native structured output for dynamic workflow subagents on supported models, new assisted approval instructions, and more reliable sign-in and permission handling. It also fixes model selection, session resume/startup behavior, Windows/macOS shell command issues, and multiple provider-specific request and image-limit problems.

  • Source: GitHub Copilot CLI releases

item.title: dotnet: Introducing dotnetup: A toolchain manager for .NET
item.description:
Microsoft introduced dotnetup, a toolchain manager for .NET on macOS and Linux. It lets developers install, manage, and update user-local .NET SDKs and runtimes.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot can now interact with desktop apps with computer use
item.description:
GitHub Copilot computer use is now in public preview in Copilot CLI and the Copilot app on macOS and Windows. It can interact with desktop applications on the user’s behalf.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Actions: macOS 14 runner image retirement
item.description:
GitHub Actions will retire the macOS 14 runner image on November 2, 2026. Before removal, jobs that use macOS 14 will temporarily fail during scheduled awareness periods.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Xcode 27 runner image now runs on macOS 27
item.description:
GitHub’s Xcode 27 runner image for GitHub-hosted macOS runners now runs on macOS 27 and is available in public preview. This lets you validate Apple apps against macOS 27 using that runner image.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Hunting MacSync Stealer infrastructure through behavioral pivots
item.description:
Microsoft describes how it tracked MacSync Stealer infrastructure despite rapid domain rotation by using stable behavioral pivots. The investigation identified more than 30 related domains.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: From open lures to cloaked gates: How a macOS ClickFix campaign learned to hide
item.description:
Microsoft describes a macOS ClickFix campaign that changed from openly delivering infostealer lures to placing them behind a browser-fingerprinting gate. The shift reduces visibility of the malicious infrastructure but also creates new detection opportunities for defenders.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog
